collect_data.description: Point one of Bright Data's site scrapers at a handful of pages and get structured records back in this step - a product with its price, stock and rating; a profile with its job history. Reach for this when the workflow needs the data now and there are tens of pages, not thousands. Bright Data allows a minute; a run that takes longer keeps going and hands back a job to pick up with 'Check a collection job'.
collect_data.display_str_template: Collect data from a site with Bright Data.
collect_data.name: collect_data

parameters.description: Which of Bright Data's scrapers to use - one per site, such as 'Amazon - Products' or 'LinkedIn - People profiles'. Pick one from the list, or paste a scraper id if it is newer than this list.
parameters.name: dataset_id

parameters.description: The page addresses to collect from, one per entry - product pages, profiles, listings. Each must start with http:// or https://. This is what almost every scraper takes; up to 1000 at a time.
parameters.name: urls

parameters.description: Use this instead of 'Pages to collect' for a scraper that takes something other than a page address - a search keyword, a category. Each entry is a set of fields, such as {"keyword": "running shoes"}. Run 'Get a scraper's fields' to see what a scraper accepts.
parameters.name: inputs

parameters.description: How this scraper should run. Leave it empty to collect the pages you name above, which is what most workflows want. The other choices discover pages first - from a keyword, a category or a best-sellers list - and then collect what they find; each one takes its own inputs, which 'Get a scraper's fields' will show you.
parameters.name: collection_method

parameters.description: Names of the fields to keep on each record, one per entry. Leave empty to get everything the scraper collects, which is often a hundred fields or more. 'Get a scraper's fields' lists the names.
parameters.name: fields

parameters.description: Caps how many records each entry above can produce. Matters for a scraper pointed at a listing or a search, where one input can produce thousands. Leave empty for no cap.
parameters.name: limit_per_input

parameters.description: Turn this on to get a row for every input the scraper could not collect, alongside the ones it could. Useful when the run has to account for every address it was given.
parameters.name: include_errors

finished.description: True when the records are in this step's result. False when the collection ran long and became a job instead

input_count.description: How many inputs this step sent

job_id.description: The job to check when 'finished' is false, and empty otherwise

items.description: One collected record. Which fields it has depends on the site - run 'Get a scraper's fields' to see them before building on them

get_job_results.description: Download the records a collection job produced. Asking before it has finished is not an error: the step comes back with 'ready' set to false and no records, so a workflow can check again on a schedule without a failed run in between.
get_job_results.display_str_template: Get a Bright Data collection job's results.
get_job_results.name: get_job_results

parameters.description: The collection job to look at. This is the id 'Start a collection job' returned - or the one 'Collect data from a site' hands back when the collection ran long enough that it stopped waiting.
parameters.name: job_id

status.description: Where the job is, when it was not ready yet

get_job_status.description: See whether a collection job has finished and whether it worked. Answers with 'finished' and 'succeeded' as well as Bright Data's own status word, so a workflow can branch on them directly - wait and check again while it is running, download the results once it is ready, and report the reason if it failed.
get_job_status.display_str_template: Check a Bright Data collection job.
get_job_status.name: get_job_status

parameters.description: The collection job to look at. This is the id 'Start a collection job' returned - or the one 'Collect data from a site' hands back when the collection ran long enough that it stopped waiting.
parameters.name: job_id

finished.description: True once the job has stopped, whether or not it worked

record_count.description: How many records it has collected

status.description: starting, running, ready, failed or canceled

succeeded.description: True only when the job finished with results to download

get_scraper_fields.description: Show what one site's scraper needs and what it gives back: the inputs it takes, which of them are required, an example you can paste straight into a collection step, and every field on a collected record. A scraper can often be run more than one way - Amazon's takes a product address, or a search keyword - and this describes one of them and lists the rest.

Returns a job id straight away; the collection keeps going on Bright Data's side, and 'Check a collection job' and 'Get collection job results' pick it up - in this workflow or in a scheduled one that runs later. Use this for hundreds or thousands of pages, where waiting in a step is not an option.

description: Get structured data out of a website without writing a scraper. Bright Data maintains ready-made scrapers for Amazon, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Google Maps and thousands of other sites: point one at some pages and get back proper fields - price, stock, rating, job history - either in the step or from a job that finishes later.
